correctness.rationale: True twins within each peripheral clique force at most one omission. For an omitted vertex from a clique of order k_i, the multiset representation has exactly k_i-1+epsilon entries equal to one, with epsilon determined only by center membership, so omitted peripheral vertices collide exactly when their clique orders agree. An omitted center has only distance-one entries, while every omitted peripheral vertex has a distance-two entry from another nontrivial clique. This proves the structural criterion; the enumerator, minimum, and basis count then follow. The checker verifies all heterogeneous windmills with peripheral order four through ten.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification on a standard block-graph construction that strictly extends the published uniform-windmill theorem. It reveals a nontrivial order-multiplicity law: each distinct peripheral clique size contributes exactly one possible omission at optimum, while repeated sizes compete. The result gives the complete resolving-set polynomial and all minimum bases, not merely a scalar parameter.
